notes.note: Tested as reject: 'mtc.running' is not allowed by the BNF (RunningOp uses ComponentOrAny, which excludes the mtc keyword). Only running is covered, not create/start/done/killed.
Release of PTC resources is not directly observable; the test only checks that the test case can be executed again after the MTC stopped itself with a connected alive PTC still running.
Removal of PTCs is observed only indirectly: a PTC that would set fail later must not influence the final verdict.
Resource release is observed via the MTC port no longer being in the Connected state (checkstate) after the PTC was killed.
Stopping exactly during an assignment cannot be forced; the PTC assigns in a loop while being stopped and the test checks that the variable is still bound afterwards.
Stopping exactly during a timer restart cannot be forced; the PTC restarts the timer in a loop while being stopped and the test checks the timer is still running afterwards.
Reject test as in the ETSI ATS (NegSem_210303_Stop_test_component_002): all component.stop in a function started on a PTC. Titan does not check this statically, hence the warning.
Reject test as in the ETSI ATS (NegSem_210304_kill_test_component_003): all component.kill in a function started on a PTC. Titan does not check this statically, hence the warning.
Ambiguity: the EXAMPLE 2 reading is chosen; all component.kill kills running, inactive and stopped alive-type PTCs as well as normal PTCs.
